clue.text: A Prime TV broadcast about airline that sucks flying at night

definitions.note: a descriptive phrase rather than a noun: the creature that sucks blood and flies at night

indicators.note: to broadcast is to scatter seed widely, so the letters are strewn into a new order
about means around, so one piece goes round another

blocks.note: the letters taken as written, to be rearranged
BA is British Airways

explanation.surface: Someone describes an Amazon Prime TV show about an airline that is frankly awful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sucks' reads as slang for being bad, but it belongs to the definition: the bat sucks blood. BA, British Airways, sits inside the rearranged letters before the final T.
explanation.definitionFit: This tropical American bat feeds on the blood of animals and hunts only after dark.

clue.text: Huge profits ultimately swallowed up by tax

indicators.note: ultimately means in the end, so only the final letter of the word is kept
something swallowed ends up inside whatever swallowed it

blocks.note: VAT is value added tax, the British sales tax
the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: A complaint that a company's enormous profits are eaten up by the taxman.
explanation.walkthrough: VAT, value added tax, is the British equivalent of a sales tax; its last two letters part to admit one letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe something of enormous size or extent, a straightforward synonym pair.

clue.text: Attractiveness of chap embracing good times at play

indicators.note: to embrace is to hug, so one piece wraps around another
things at play are moving about freely, so the letters shift into a new order

blocks.note: a chap is a man
G is the standard abbreviation for good
taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A man's charm comes from the fun he has when enjoying himself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Good times' looks like one phrase, but good is just G, tucked into the chap, while times is the anagram fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Magnetism is used figuratively for personal charm or allure that draws other people in.

clue.text: Opening bars: penny off pint, unlimited grog

indicators.note: off means removed, so the named letter comes away from the word
without limits means without its boundaries, so the end letters go and the middle stays

blocks.note: P, the abbreviation for a penny, is the letter to drop
the word with its P taken away
the word without its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A pub's opening bars offer a penny off a pint and unlimited grog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Opening bars' suggests pubs opening their doors, but it means the first bars of a piece of music. Grog is rum and water, or loosely any drink.
explanation.definitionFit: An intro is the short opening passage of a song or tune, played before the main melody begins.

clue.text: Former lover, generously proportioned model

blocks.note: an ex is a former partner
ample means large or plentiful

explanation.surface: Someone's ex-partner is described as a model with a full figure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Model' looks like a fashion model, but it means a pattern to follow.
explanation.definitionFit: A model in the sense of a pattern worth copying is an example others should follow.

clue.text: Endlessly esteem a student officer of the navy

indicators.note: without an end, the word loses its final letter

blocks.note: to esteem is to admire, here cut short
taken as written
L for learner, as on British learner-driver plates

explanation.surface: A student naval officer is held in endless high regard.
explanation.walkthrough: Student giving L is a crossword convention from the L-plates British learner drivers display.
explanation.definitionFit: An admiral is the most senior rank of commissioned officer in a naval fleet.

clue.text: Obscene material corporation’s withdrawn

indicators.note: withdrawing is pulling back, so the letters travel backwards

blocks.note: a corporation is jocular old slang for a paunch, a tum
the possessive taken as written

explanation.surface: A company has pulled some offensive content.
explanation.walkthrough: Corporation reads as a business; in crosswords it is also old slang for a pot belly.
explanation.definitionFit: Smut is indecent or pornographic writing or pictures, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Confused conflict – Middle East’s leaders shelter

indicators.note: leaders are those at the front, so the first letters are taken

blocks.note: the opening letter of each word
the lee is the sheltered side, away from the wind

explanation.surface: News of a muddled war where regional leaders take cover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Middle East' could also give ME as a plain abbreviation; either way the same two letters lead.
explanation.definitionFit: A melee is a disorderly scuffle or brawl involving many people at close quarters.

clue.text: Working on best hardwood, choice cut

indicators.note: placed on here means set within, so one piece is put inside the next

blocks.note: a machine that is working is on
taken as written
teak is a tropical hardwood

explanation.surface: A carpenter selects a fine cut of the best hardwood to work on.
explanation.walkthrough: Two nested insertions: the working piece goes inside best, and that lot inside the hardwood.
explanation.definitionFit: A T-bone is a prime cut of beef with a T-shaped bone, so a quality cut from the butcher.

clue.text: Competent English queen escorted by a romantic partner

A as written plus DATE, someone you go out with

explanation.surface: A capable English queen arrives on the arm of her beloved.
explanation.walkthrough: The queen here is QU rather than the more usual ER or R.
explanation.definitionFit: Competent in the sense of satisfactory, good enough for the purpose, matches adequate.

clue.text: Quote talking sense

blocks.note: to quote a source is to cite it

explanation.surface: Someone quotes what sounds like plain common sense.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Talking sense' reads as a phrase, but sense is the definition and talking signals the sound.
explanation.definitionFit: Vision is one of the five bodily senses alongside hearing, smell, touch and taste.

clue.text: American Republican, crazy sick old Texan resident?

blocks.note: A is the abbreviation for American
R is the abbreviation for Republican
mad means crazy
ill means sick

explanation.surface: A deranged, unwell Republican politician who once lived in Texas.
explanation.walkthrough: The picture is a human Texan; the question mark warns that the resident is an animal.
explanation.definitionFit: The armoured armadillo is native to Texas and is the state's official small mammal.

clue.text: Having dislocated elbow, dad runs off

indicators.note: a dislocated joint is knocked out of place, so these letters are moved out of order

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.walkthrough: 'Runs off' looks like a phrasal verb, but runs is R and off is the definition, meaning unwell.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling off means slightly unwell, and below par is an idiom for not in normal health.

clue.text: Manuel’s gag starts to upset enraged line of Americans

definitions.note: a cryptic phrase: queue is the British word for what Americans call a line

indicators.note: starts are beginnings, so the first letter of each following word is taken

blocks.note: Manuel, the Spanish waiter in Fawlty Towers, has the catchphrase 'Que?'
the opening letter of each word

explanation.surface: Manuel's joke upsets and angers a row of American tourists.
explanation.walkthrough: Fawlty Towers is a classic BBC sitcom; Manuel, its bewildered Spanish waiter, answers everything with 'Que?'. 'Line of Americans' means what Americans call a line.
explanation.definitionFit: Americans stand in line where British people stand in a queue, so the two are regional equivalents.

clue.text: Extemporised notes of stereotypical WI meeting?

blocks.note: first meaning: an improvised musical get-together
second meaning, whimsical: a gathering spent making fruit preserves

explanation.walkthrough: The WI is the Women's Institute, a British women's organisation famous for making preserves, so its typical gathering is pictured as a session spent on jam.
explanation.definitionFit: Musicians improvising together informally hold a jam session, and the WI's preserve-making reputation supplies the second reading.

clue.text: Give life to a new friend touring Italy

indicators.note: to tour is to travel round, so the pieces go around another

blocks.note: taken as written
N is the abbreviation for new
I is the international vehicle code for Italy
a mate is a friend

explanation.surface: A fresh companion on a trip around Italy brings someone back to life.
explanation.walkthrough: Italy is I from its international car registration code, a common crossword convention.
explanation.definitionFit: To animate something is to bring it to life or make it lively and moving.

clue.text: Advanced tricky game daughter condensed

blocks.note: A is the abbreviation for advanced, as in A level
bridge is a card game played in tricks
D is the abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: A difficult game for experts, made shorter for a daughter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tricky' suggests difficult, but bridge is a game won by taking tricks.
explanation.definitionFit: An abridged book or text has been shortened while keeping its essential content.

clue.text: Perrins’s saucy partner left dodgy marketing material

indicators.note: something dodgy is unreliable or not as it should be, so the letters are put wrong

blocks.note: Lea & Perrins is the famous brand of Worcestershire sauce
taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Perrins's cheeky business partner walked out over shady advertising.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Saucy' sounds like cheeky but literally means sauce: Lea and Perrins make Worcestershire sauce. 'Left' is fodder, not a departure.
explanation.definitionFit: A leaflet is a printed sheet handed out to advertise or promote goods and services.

clue.text: Improved security devices from Spooner where the envelope is pushed?

indicators.note: Reverend Spooner famously swapped the opening sounds of words, so initial sounds are exchanged

blocks.note: improved means better
locks keep doors secure
swap the opening B and L sounds

explanation.surface: Stronger locks invented by Spooner, for the place where boundaries get tested.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pushing the envelope' is an idiom for testing limits, but here an envelope is literally pushed through the door slot.
explanation.definitionFit: Mail is delivered by pushing envelopes through the slot in a front door, which is the letterbox.

clue.text: Japanese warrior knocked back booze in Asia sozzled

indicators.note: knocked back pushes something backwards, so the letters run the other way
sozzled means very drunk, so the letters reel about into a new order
in places one piece within another

blocks.note: rum is an alcoholic spirit
taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A drunken Japanese warrior downed his drink somewhere in Asia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Knocked back' reads as drinking up, but it signals reversal of the drink.
explanation.definitionFit: The samurai were the hereditary military class of feudal Japan, sworn to serve their lords.

clue.text: Confused again as Pinochet’s accepted

indicators.note: what is accepted is taken in, so the answer lies held within the words

blocks.note: the letters run across the word boundaries

explanation.surface: Someone is bewildered once more, as the Chilean dictator Pinochet admitted.
explanation.walkthrough: Pinochet was the military ruler of Chile; his name is there only to supply letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in a spin is an idiom for being agitated, flustered or thoroughly confused.

clue.text: Lethargy of Maître Nicolas following retirement

indicators.note: of here means taken from, so the answer is drawn out of the words

blocks.note: the letters straddle the two words

explanation.walkthrough: Maître is the French title for a lawyer; 'retirement' sounds like leaving work but tells you to read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Inertia is a tendency to do nothing or remain inactive, a close synonym of sluggish listlessness.

clue.text: Endanger sovereign when evacuating area

indicators.note: to evacuate is to empty out or leave, so the named letter departs

blocks.note: imperial, as in sovereign or ruling, minus one A
A is the abbreviation for area, the letter removed

explanation.surface: A monarch is put at risk while an area is being cleared.
explanation.walkthrough: Sovereign is read as an adjective here, meaning imperial, rather than as a king or coin.
explanation.definitionFit: To imperil someone is to put them in peril, exposing them to danger or harm.

clue.text: Quiet road circling a London landmark

taken as written
RD is the abbreviation for road

explanation.walkthrough: Quiet and road together form the outer pair, with the article sitting between them.
explanation.definitionFit: The Shard is the tall glass skyscraper near London Bridge, the tallest building in Britain.

clue.text: Abolish yearbook after deleting its second article

indicators.note: deleting means striking out, so a letter is taken away

explanation.walkthrough: 'Article' looks like a magazine piece, but it is the word A; ANNUAL has two, and the later one goes.
explanation.definitionFit: To annul a law or marriage is to declare it void, effectively abolishing it.

clue.text: Debut for Apple phablet leading with large range of letters

clue.text: Collect first seen in Anglican service

clue.text: Warning sign seen at hen night?

clue.text: Private guarding tower, one in charge of The Crown?
